text:
Henry's total trip is 60 miles. His first stop is after 20 miles, so it is 20 miles from the start. His second stop is 15 miles before the end, so it is 60 - 15 = 45 miles from the start. The distance between the two stops is 45 - 20 = 25 miles.

Answer: 25
reasoning:
We are given: "Henry made two stops during his 60-mile bike trip. He first stopped after 20 miles. His second stop was 15 miles before the end of the trip. How many miles did he travel between his first and second stops?"

Total trip = 60 miles.
First stop: after 20 miles (so distance from start to first stop = 20 miles).
Second stop: 15 miles before the end of the trip (so distance from second stop to end = 15 miles). Therefore, the distance from start to second stop = 60 - 15 = 45 miles.
Distance between first stop and second stop = distance from start to second stop - distance from start to first stop = 45 - 20 = 25 miles.

Answer: 25 miles.
